programme.title: Piel Salvaje
programme.desc: In the letters that Henry delivered to Max, Rosa Blanco says that her daughter was taken from her and Camila, very anxious, believes that she will finally know why her mother abandoned her. Marcelina finds the box with the letters and upon learning the contents, altered, orders them to be burned.

programme.title: Piel Salvaje
programme.desc: The letters contain evidence incriminating Patricia and Fausto in Leoncio's murder. Camila will make important decisions, especially to find the four women who betrayed her mother. Fausto has a serious intention: Rosa Blanco must be killed.

programme.title: Piel Salvaje
programme.desc: Mother Isabel confirms to Camila part of the secrets she is hiding: Patricia and her sister-in-law Maria Amelia were the ones who denounced her mother. Luciano receives an envelope containing a photo of Camila as a child, with her little yellow dress, and behind it, a woman protecting her.

programme.title: Piel Salvaje
programme.desc: The four women who destroyed Rosa Blanco's life meet again in an empty house. Camila confronts Fausto accusing Patricia of being Leoncio's murderer. Once again a motorist warns her not to keep looking for her mother and snatches her letter.

programme.title: Piel Salvaje
programme.desc: Much confusion in Camila, nothing justifies the lies and Camila is increasingly disappointed in Mother Isabel's deceptions. Ezequiel confronts Julia and savagely assaults Gregorio when they are found together.

programme.title: Piel Salvaje
programme.desc: Mother Isabel confesses to Camila but the girl knows she is still lying. Jeli, her little sister, suffers because of Fernando's irresponsibility, who impregnated her. Max announces to Marcelina and Astrid that he will soon marry Camila.

programme.title: Piel Salvaje
programme.desc: Fausto hires Anton, a criminal, to assassinate Rosa Blanco; Camila and Max, happy, tell Father Tiziano about their upcoming wedding. programme.desc: Max is too hurt and no longer believes in that love, warning her that from now on he will hate her, forget her and that she will be the victim of his own decision. Blind with anger and pain, he shouts to those present to leave because there will be no wedding.

programme.title: Piel Salvaje

programme.desc: Camila explains to Ezequiel and Julia the reason for her happiness: she will marry Max, and will also soon be reunited with her mother. programme.title: Piel Salvaje
programme.desc: Camila spots a woman matching her mother's description. Anton, the hitman, is also there and armed, he goes to them. Torrealba orders his men to run to the women, grab Camila and take the woman away.

programme.desc: Simone about a forced sabbatical, what keeps her busy these days, the starting point of the new album Omega, writing together in the same room, finding the musical direction, revisiting Design Your Universe, The Skeleton Key, dreams and nightmares, fame vs privacy, Omega being a very diverse album, the Omega point, light vs darkness, Freedom – The Wolves Within, looking back at their earlier work, working with Ayreon on Transitus.

programme.title: P.J. Morton interview
programme.desc: P.J. about the music he grew up with, the first song he ever wrote, his early career and learning about the industry, delving into production, his sound, digging deeper on Watch The Sun, his computer crashing, how the lockdowns influenced the album, Be Like Water, working with Nas and Stevie Wonder, Please Don’t Walk Away, catharsis through songwriting

programme.title: DMA's interview - Tommy O'Dell
programme.desc: Tommy about their show at the Brixton Academy and Liam Gallagher, finding his voice, the album Glow, dance elements, writing lyrics, Silver, staying true to yourself, ambition, not trying to please everyone, Never Before, Criminals and pop, songs that evolve on the road, Life is a Game of Changing, what he learned as a frontman.

programme.title: Beth Hart interview
programme.desc: Beth about learning from gardening, magical moments, addressing personal issues, facing your problems and taking responsibility, singing Led Zeppelin songs, healing through music, recording vocals, Stairway To Heaven and No Quarter, getting honest feedback, other artists she would like to cover, writing new songs of her own, trying new things, being willing to fail and learn, her love for the Netherlands.

programme.title: Alvaro Soler interview
programme.desc: Álvaro about his new album Magia, contrast in his music, summer holiday memories, positive songs, getting back into producing, experimentation in the writing process, displaying his diversity, En Tu Piel, writing from experience, Tipo Normal, feeling useless without live shows, the title Magia

programme.title: Declan McKenna interview
programme.desc: Declan about his album Zeros, finding his place in music, playfulness, making observations about society, a positive sense of humanity, Daniel You’re Still a Child, The Social Dilemma documentary, turning off his notifications, the good and bad of social media, organic and raw sounds, good mistakes, capturing the right energy on the album, trusting yourself as a musician, taking control, finally getting the album out, his favorite lyric on the album.

programme.title: Interview with Carrie Underwood
programme.desc: An Interview with Carrie Underwood

programme.title: Fish interview
programme.desc: Fish about keeping busy during luckdown, working on the Weltschmerz album, Script for a Jester’s Tear saving his ass, growing vegetables, looking for silver linings, the global economy, the health services, climate change, where the idea for Weltschmerz came from, his character driven style of writing, mental health, Grace of God, his retirement from music, Marillion getting too big, knowing what he wants to make, taking his time, being tough on his own lyrics, leaving people wanting more, doing a double album, never having been financially motivated, doing exactly what you want.

programme.title: Jason Mraz and his cat
programme.desc: Jason about feeling priveledged during social distancing, Gratitude, taking the good with the bad, using music to combat depression, what makes a song great, reggae music, his new album Look For The Good, You Do You, self-acceptance and mindfulness, our common humanity.

programme.title: St. Vincent interview
programme.desc: Annie about how she started in music, creative expression, the sound of the early 70s, writing for her new album Daddy’s Home, writing about flawed people, Somebody Like Me, finding stillness for the first time, not worrying about the commercial side, signing an autograph in prison, why she decided to write about the incarceration of her father, the Wurlitzer, working with Jack Antonoff, the various ways of writing songs, knowing when a song is done, performing at SNL.

programme.title: Cindy Blackman interview
programme.desc: Cindy about The Quarantine Blues, a chance to reset, becoming better humans, her love for the drums, always looking to improve, singing a lot on the new album Give The Drummer Some, We Came To Play, Mother Earth, sharing music, bringing jazz to more people, not putting music into boxes, inspiration, the incredible jazz musicians she learned from, enjoying the little things.

programme.title: James Arthur interview
programme.desc: James about music as a sanctuary, anxiety, his first real song Grey Skies, his songwriting roots, the new record You, letting go of pressure, reinventing himself, Marine Parade, the beauty of being a solo artist, leaving songs open for interpretation, the title track You, being fine with who you are, how he sees success, Glastonbury.

programme.title: Interview with Damien Jurado
programme.desc: An Interview with Damien Jurado

programme.title: Steven Wilson interview
programme.desc: Steven about releasing an album during the pandemic, falling out of love with the guitar, the origins of his new album The Future Bites, living in an electronic world, Eddie van Halen, King Ghost, an exciting songwriting process, making the characters he writes about believable, creativity and technology, the internet changing human nature, the decline of truth and reality, positive change, the year 2032 an consumer culture, curiosity being under threat.

programme.title: Interview with Bring Me The Horizon
programme.desc: An Interview with Bring Me The Horizon

programme.title: Interview with Blossoms
programme.desc: An Interview with Blossoms

programme.title: Bedrugs and PurplePill sing Wave
programme.desc: Bedrugs and PurplePill sing Wave

programme.title: Interview with Billie Eilish
programme.desc: An Interview with Billie Eilish

programme.title: Countain Crows interview - Adam Duritz
programme.desc: Adam about visiting his friends farm in England, shaving his head, starting on the Butter Miracle EP, music being a personal thing for him, Tall Grass, the evolution of his songwriting, the ghosts from your childhood, learning how to live, a screw-up with the release, working on a second Butter Miracle suite, keeping true to the song, a trumpet solo, the album getting so much support, feeling responsible for his crew.

programme.title: Guy Sebastian interview
programme.desc: Guy about coping with the global pandemic, how Australia is handling it, a historically significant time, reflecting on his life and career, realizing what’s important, Before I Go, a messy management betrayal, creativity during lockdown, silver linings, adding positivity to the world, the song Choir for his friend who passed away, a beautiful moment, Standing With You, the importance of mental health, having his sons on the album, gaining strength from the people around him, Believer, T.R.U.T.H

programme.title: Blood Red Shoes interview - Steven Ansell
programme.desc: Steven about not fitting in in Brighton, the punk spirit, dealing with the lockdown, Laura learning to drive, the tone of the new album Ghosts On Tape, MORBID FASCINATION, stripped down tracks, lyric writing, I AM NOT YOU, not being able to play live, pride for what they have accomplished, the secret of longevity, serial killer podcasts and documentaries.

programme.title: Larkin Poe_interview
programme.desc: Rebecca and Megan about playing for change, the power of music, unlearning some of their musical upbringing, trusting themselves, forging their own path, five years of growth, going to Nashville to record Blood Harmony, the art of pre-production, sibling harmonies, still surprising each other, ambition

programme.title: Joe Satriani interview
programme.desc: Joe about when he was still a beginner on guitar, working hard to get better, NYC in the early 70s, the surrealness of his career, teaching Steve Vai, finding “work-arounds” as a guitar player, Eddie van Halen, The Elephants of Mars, experimentation, composing songs over the internet, songs coming together organically, a song inspired by Questlove, Randy Rhoads and what keeps inspiring him.

programme.title: Eefje de Visser interview
programme.desc: Eefje over haar nieuwe plaat Bitterzoet, muziek voor in de auto, schrijven vanuit piano, haar thuisstudio, niet te braaf willen zijn, een internationaal gevoel, altijd beginnen bij de muziek, kritisch zijn op haar eigen teksten, beeldvorming, tegenstellingen, vluchten uit de realiteit, verloren potentie, zelf-bewustzijn, vol inspiratie zitten.

programme.title: Jean-Michel Jarre interview
programme.desc: Jean-Michel about Welcome To The Other Side, a virtual Notre Dame, the impact of the pandemic on music, innovations in music technology, binaural recording, VR and augmented reality as new forms of expression, the value of music, respecting intellectual property, this being only the beginning of the digital age, artificial intelligence, Ray Charles and Pierre Soulages, lessons from his mother, a street in Lyon being named after his mother

programme.title: Headline：A Chinese village run by a CEO
programme.desc:
In a Dai village called "Manluanzhan" near China's southwestern border, a full-time rural CEO manages the books and coordinates business operations at homestays, cafés, breweries, and other shops. But how to benefit from rural tourism without losing the village charm?
In Manluanzhan, a fresh experiment is unfolding – one where villagers remain participants, investors, and decision-makers, but a CEO enters the fray to help defend their interests.

programme.title: Meet China: Starting Green, Reaching the Future
programme.desc: In this episode of Meet China, wind becomes more than a natural force—it powers a greener future across China and Europe. A piece of fabric reveals how Chinese innovation is reshaping global perceptions of manufacturing. Ancient ruins in central China are reimagined as immersive cultural experiences, turning heritage into living memory. And in Laos, Chinese agricultural expertise is helping farmers unlock higher yields and new opportunities. From energy and textiles to tourism and farming, this episode shows how innovation is renewing tradition and connecting futures across borders.

From tourism to business partnerships, the world's top sporting event is bringing people, markets and ideas closer together. But what does it take to turn global exposure into long-term growth? And what are the new trends shaping sports marketing? Join us on BizTalk as we explore the business opportunities behind "the beautiful game."

programme.title: Meet China: Turning Villages into Stages, Taking Creativity to the World
programme.desc: In this episode of Meet China, we step into the frontlines of rural revitalization to see how a Gen-Z village chief is breathing new life into her hometown. programme.desc:

programme.title: China's Industrial Chains: Threads of Resilience
programme.desc: What is clothing made from? Not just cotton or wool. Sometimes, it starts with a single drop of oil! Follow CGTN as we reveal how a drop of crude oil transforms into our clothes, uncovering a complex and fascinating journey of the textile and garment manufacturing process. Follow CGTN's Wang Tianyu and take a closer look at China's textile and garment industry, and unravel the threads that connect China's industrial past, present and future.

programme.desc: In this episode of Meet China, we step into the frontlines of rural revitalization to see how a Gen-Z village chief is breathing new life into her hometown. We then visit the world’s toy capital, where Chinese manufacturing is turning culture and creativity into global stories. From a green beef cycle near Beijing to rice-prawn co-culture in Cambodia, this episode explores how technology, industry and cooperation are helping land thrive and livelihoods grow.

programme.title: BizTalk | AI talent race and the future of work
programme.desc: As artificial intelligence (AI) transforms industries worldwide, competition in AI is increasingly driven not only by technology, but also by talent, skills and workforce development. In this episode of BizTalk, CGTN's Lily Lyu speaks with industry leaders and universities, to explore how AI is reshaping talent demand across industries, and how China is building a broader AI talent pipeline for the future.

programme.title: Innovating at Scale: Behind the Scenes of AMNC26
programme.desc:
Ahead of the World Economic Forum's (WEF) Annual Meeting of the New Champions, or known as the "Summer Davos" in Dalian, CGTN’s Michael Wang speaks with three key WEF organizers to explore what it takes to scale innovation in a rapidly changing world.
This special discussion offers an exclusive behind-the-scenes look at how the WEF brings together innovators, businesses and policymakers to turn ideas into real-world change.

programme.title: China's Industrial Chains: Threads of Resilience
programme.desc: What is clothing made from? Not just cotton or wool. Sometimes, it starts with a single drop of oil! Follow CGTN as we reveal how a drop of crude oil transforms into our clothes, uncovering a complex and fascinating journey of the textile and garment manufacturing process. Follow CGTN's Wang Tianyu and take a closer look at China's textile and garment industry, and unravel the threads that connect China's industrial past, present and future.

programme.title: Oh Dior!
programme.desc: Sabbatical Entertainment's exclusive original documentary admires Christian Dior, the famous French fashion designer whose post-World War II creations were wildly popular and whose legacy continues to influence the fashion industry.

programme.title: Yves Saint Laurent - Firestarter
programme.desc: We explore YSL's unparalleled professional acclaim, as well as his fascinating and tumultuous personal life. YSL was able to adapt his style to accommodate the changes in fashion during his entire career. He approached fashion with a different narrative by wanting women to look comfortable yet elegant at the same time.

programme.title: Yves Saint Laurent -Creador De Fuego
programme.desc: We explore YSL's unparalleled professional acclaim, as well as his fascinating and tumultuous personal life. YSL was able to adapt his style to accommodate the changes in fashion during his entire career. He approached fashion with a different narrative by wanting women to look comfortable yet elegant at the same time.

programme.title: Andy Warhol Fluorescent
programme.desc: Warhol, evolutionary and controversial, was never afraid to break the mold and reshape the reals of art, advertising, & directing. But who was the real man being behind the colors in which he hid? Was it the art or the fame that controlled & spawned his unique creativity? Sabbatical Entertainment takes an in-depth look at the life and works of Andy Warhol.

programme.title: Crazy For Madonna
programme.desc: A biography of a universal icon of music and Hollywood, Madonna, better known as the Queen of Pop. Sabbatical Entertainment celebrates Madonna’s illustrious career spanning more than four decades, always pushing the boundaries of entertainment. Not afraid of controversy, the Material girl, through her talents, redefined pop culture history.

programme.title: Eastwood
programme.desc: Pay homage to Clint Eastwood, the oldest living cinematic icon. Success did not come easy for Eastwood, but throughout his career he has reaped numerous triumphs, directed more than 44 films, and acted in more than 72... Winner of over 150 awards including four Oscars, the iconic Eastwood has not only secured his place in the history of Hollywood, but in the history of world cinema. Bravo!!!

programme.title: For Our Eyes Only
programme.desc: In anticipation of the 25th chapter in the iconic James Bond Saga, Sabbatical Entertainment presents an enthralling documentary that recounts & relives all of 007’s menacing missions throughout this legendary cinematic franchise, from “Dr. No”, to the highly anticipated “No Time To Die.” Get to know the actors who have embodied the super spy: Connery, Lazenby, Moore, Dalton, Brosnan, and Craig, their similarities & the characteristics that differentiate each one when exhibiting 007’s well-known charm, class and elegance, combined with his physical and mental prowess, that make James Bond, a real life super hero.

programme.title: Sky's The Limit
programme.desc: A documentary exploring the muralist movement: the art of painting over breathtaking heights. Windowless gable walls were graffiti painters’ early targets, particularly in urban areas under renovation, and since 2012, monumental graffiti is in full rebirth especially in Paris’ 13th arrondissement. Through a design thought as a décor, obliterating the blandness of the walls, artists skillfully revive these soulless surfaces.

programme.title: Dances with the Wind
programme.desc: ‘Fury Dance’ is a story about a Korean protest dancer, Sam-hun Lee. He fought for the democratization of South Korea in the ‘80’s through dance, while giving up his own dream to become a ballerino. The film takes the viewer through prominent events in South Korean history, as Sam-hun dances to soothe the souls of victims who were killed by the Korean national violence during the past 30 years. During the 1980 Gwangju Massacre however, Sam-hun developed a panic disorder. So he crosses through the Eurasian rail with difficulty when invited to attend a festival to dance in France. Through his journey, he attempts to overcome his claustrophobic fears in France, revisits his lost dream of becoming a ballerino in Russia, and dances for the Holocaust victims in Poland. Documented for 15 years, this film is dedicated to those who lost their noble lives while fighting for freedom against the unjust political power.

programme.title: Frank & Fearless
programme.desc: An aging reprobate, a rural boy, a large dog and an orphaned baby rhino set out to stop the rhino slaughter. Their quest buffets them between high comedy and searing tragedy, until they end up an inspiration and a conscience to a world in need of heroes.

programme.title: Running Funny
programme.desc: Michael and Eddie are two broke college graduates who rent an “apartment” from Stan, a cantankerous blind war veteran. As they begin their tumultuous transition into the real world, they quickly discover that finding a job will be more complex than securing their degrees.

programme.title: Cabin of Errors
programme.desc: When Peter and Nancy split up, their friends plot to bring them back together during a trip to a cabin. But things go hilariously wrong when Peter comes to the cabin with other intentions. A modern day romantic comedy farce.

programme.title: 1st Bite
programme.desc: Set on a tropical island in Thailand, the strange plight of a beleaguered chef who, while romancing a mysterious woman, discovers the diabolical Zen of cooking. Following a near death escape, he returns to Montreal and falls hard for the woman of his life who unfortunately craves only his cooking but not his loving. Worse still, strange things surfacing around him indicate that his journey to the Far East has deep, divine implications. The stage is set for him to take the 1st bite of true love and end the cycle of suffering for all involved.

programme.title: Afrontar la adolescencia de tus hijos, Duelo emocional de las madre, Momento de DESmadre Podcast
programme.desc:
En este episodio de Momento de DESmadre, conversamos con la terapeuta familiar Erika Ángulo sobre uno de los temas más desafiantes para muchas madres: la adolescencia de los hijos y el duelo emocional que sentimos al verlos crecer y empezar a soltarse de nuestra mano.
Hablamos sobre cómo manejar la etapa de la "aborrecencia", entender los cambios emocionales y de comportamiento de los adolescentes, y cómo las mamás podemos vivir este proceso sin tanta culpa, con herramientas que nos ayuden a conectar desde el amor y la empatía.
💬 Temas que tocamos:
Cómo lidiar con la adolescencia de los hijos Qué es el duelo emocional en la maternidad Cambios emocionales en los adolescentes Cómo soltar y dejar crecer a los hijos sin dolor Consejos de una terapeuta familiar para madres 🎧 Escucha, comparte y acompáñanos en este momento de reflexión y desahogo maternal. ¡No estás sola!
🔔 Suscríbete para más conversaciones reales, sin filtros y con mucho DESmadre.
#Adolescencia #MaternidadReal #PodcastParaMujeres #DueloMaternal #MomentoDeDESmadre #ErikaÁngulo #Adolescentes #Familia #PodcastEnEspañol

programme.title: ¿Las pantallas están criando a tus hijos? Sol Macaluso y Fátima de Francisco en Matronas al Rescate
programme.desc:
uevo programa de Matronas al Rescate en Canal Barro — y esta vez tocamos uno de los temas más urgentes: cómo las pantallas, las redes sociales y la inteligencia artificial están afectando a la infancia.
Las invitadas de lujo fueron: 💬 Sol Macaluso, periodista e influencer, que compartió su experiencia personal de crianza en tiempos digitales. 📚 Fátima de Francisco, especialista en educación y crianza, que nos habló de los riesgos y efectos reales del uso de pantallas y recomendó libros imprescindibles para madres y padres.
Además: 🍼 Desmontamos trucos virales para dormir bebés, 🧠 debatimos sobre educación sexual y responsabilidad digital, 😱 y Fátima nos dejó helados con un dato impactante: el vídeo pornográfico más descargado de 2017 fue el de “La Manada”, una muestra brutal de la falta de educación sexual y empatía social que seguimos arrastrando.
Un programa necesario, incómodo, pero urgente. 👉 Matronas al Rescate, todos los jueves a las 11:00 AM (España) en YouTube Canal Barro.
#MatronasAlRescate #SolMacaluso #FatimaDeFrancisco #EducacionSexual #Pantallas #CrianzaDigital #CanalBarro #IA #InfanciaDigital

programme.title: Reinventarse como mujer, mamá y artista: Jessi León en Momento de Desmadre Podcast
programme.desc:
En este episodio de Momento de Desmadre, hablamos con la cantautora argentina @TheJessileon León, mitad del dúo Periko & Jessi León, sobre cómo la maternidad transformó su vida y su música.
Jessi nos cuenta cómo ella y Periko decidieron reinventarse completamente tras convertirse en padres. Junto a su hijo Milo, están lanzando un nuevo disco @pjkidsOfficial una recopilación de canciones inéditas para niños, grabadas desde su casa, en familia y con mucho amor.
Hablamos de cómo la maternidad no solo nos cambia, sino que nos abre la mente para crear cosas absolutamente maravillosas. Desde los desafíos emocionales hasta los momentos de inspiración profunda, este episodio es un testimonio de resiliencia, amor y creatividad.
No olvides suscribirte, dejar tu comentario y compartir este video con esa mamá, artista o persona creativa que necesita escucharlo.
#MomentoDeDesmadre #JessiLeón #PerikoyJessiLeón #MaternidadCreativa #DiscoInfantil #Reinvención #PodcastEnEspañol #MúsicaDesdeCasa #MamáArtista

programme.title: 🌍 La responsabilidad de cuidar el planeta | Con Marly Boscan Molins 🌱
programme.desc:
En este episodio de Momento de Desmadre con Marly Boscan Molins sobre un tema que nos toca a todos: el cuidado del planeta.
Marly nos comparte cómo podemos hacer una diferencia desde nuestro hogar, con acciones simples pero poderosas que impactan directamente el medio ambiente.
💚 Hablamos de sostenibilidad, del poder del ejemplo en la familia, y de cómo cada pequeña decisión cuenta. Porque cuidar la Tierra no es solo una causa global, es una responsabilidad personal y cotidiana.
✨ ¡Dale play, suscríbete y comparte este mensaje con quienes también quieren ser parte del cambio!
🔔 No olvides activar la campanita para no perderte los próximos episodios.
👇 Cuéntanos en los comentarios: ¿Qué haces tú desde casa para cuidar el planeta?
#MomentoDeDesmadre #CuidadoDelPlaneta #Sostenibilidad #diadelatierra #latierraeslacasadetodos #latierra #PodcastLatino #MarlyBoscanMolins #EcoMoms #CambiaElMundoDesdeCasa #podcastlatino #podcastenespañol

programme.title: Diana Arango: Cómo emprender desde cero, ser mamá y crear una empresa exitosa
programme.desc:
En este episodio de Momento de Desmadre, tengo una conversación poderosa con Diana Arango, fundadora y CEO de Chefpost, una plataforma innovadora que nació durante la pandemia y hoy conecta a chefs profesionales con personas que quieren comer saludable y sin complicaciones desde casa.
Diana nos comparte cómo fue ese salto al emprendimiento desde su necesidad personal, cómo logró levantar una empresa rentable mientras criaba a sus hijos, y cómo ha creado una red de apoyo para otras mujeres emprendedoras.
Hablamos de negocios, maternidad, liderazgo femenino y el valor de emprender con propósito. Si estás pensando en lanzar tu propio negocio, si ya estás emprendiendo o si simplemente quieres llenarte de inspiración real y sin filtros… este episodio es para ti.
🌟 Sobre Chefpost: Chefpost es una plataforma que permite a las personas contratar chefs profesionales para cocinar en casa de manera personalizada, saludable y práctica. También es una oportunidad para que chefs independientes puedan trabajar con libertad y hacer crecer su negocio.
🔗 Conecta con Diana y Chefpost: 🌐 https://chefpost.com 📸 Instagram: @chefpost | @dianaarangoc
📲 Sígueme para más contenido real y sin filtros sobre maternidad, emprendimiento y desmadre: Instagram: @paulazelaya_ Website: https://paulazelaya.com

programme.title: Reinventarse en silla de ruedas con Didi Chacon
programme.desc:
Hoy en Momento de Desmadre hablamos con Diana Chacón, mejor conocida como Didi, actriz, modelo y presentadora venezolana.
Durante la pandemia, su vida dio un giro inesperado: tras recibir la vacuna contra el COVID, sufrió efectos secundarios que la dejaron en silla de ruedas y con pérdida de memoria.
Pero lo que parecía el final, se convirtió en el inicio de una nueva versión de sí misma. Didi nos cuenta cómo recuperó su autoestima, su memoria y su pasión por la vida, demostrando que reinventarse es posible, incluso en los momentos más oscuros.
Una conversación que te va a sacudir el alma y te va a llenar de fuerza.
🎧 Disponible ya en Spotify, Apple Podcasts y todas las plataformas. ✨ No te lo pierdas.

programme.title: Carta astral de ROSALÍA y RAUW ALEJANDRO: ¿Por qué no funcionó su amor? | Ministerio de Brujas
programme.desc:
Bienvenidas al aquelarre semanal de Ministerio de Brujas, el programa más místico, salvaje y necesario de Canal Barro. Como todos los martes a las 19h (España), encendimos la hoguera para prender fuego a todo lo que sobra… y esta vez, ardieron los sin código (sí, los que intentan ligar con la pareja de su amiga) y los algoritmos que manipulan nuestras vidas.
💘 En la Secretaría de Venus en Tanga, una joven asistente sacó carta del tarot erótico (y el estudio se volvió un sauna cósmico). ♏ Chongazen leyó el clima astral de la semana escorpiana, entre pasiones, celos y renacimientos. 🎬 Fernanda, desde el Departamento de Cine, recomendó Years and Years y Los Domingos, dos obras sobre el fin del mundo y las segundas oportunidades. 💫 Pero lo más esperado fue el análisis de la carta astral de ROSALÍA (recién lanzando álbum) y RAUW ALEJANDRO. Las brujas compararon sus planetas, sus Venus, sus Plutones… y entendieron por qué el amor se les fue por el ascendente.
✨ Un episodio entre fuego, deseo y astrología pop. Suscríbete, que en Ministerio de Brujas, cada martes arde algo nuevo.

programme.title: Reinventarse como mujer, mamá y artista: Jessi León en Momento de Desmadre Podcast
programme.desc:
En este episodio de Momento de Desmadre, hablamos con la cantautora argentina @TheJessileon León, mitad del dúo Periko & Jessi León, sobre cómo la maternidad transformó su vida y su música.
Jessi nos cuenta cómo ella y Periko decidieron reinventarse completamente tras convertirse en padres. Junto a su hijo Milo, están lanzando un nuevo disco @pjkidsOfficial una recopilación de canciones inéditas para niños, grabadas desde su casa, en familia y con mucho amor.
Hablamos de cómo la maternidad no solo nos cambia, sino que nos abre la mente para crear cosas absolutamente maravillosas. Desde los desafíos emocionales hasta los momentos de inspiración profunda, este episodio es un testimonio de resiliencia, amor y creatividad.
No olvides suscribirte, dejar tu comentario y compartir este video con esa mamá, artista o persona creativa que necesita escucharlo.
#MomentoDeDesmadre #JessiLeón #PerikoyJessiLeón #MaternidadCreativa #DiscoInfantil #Reinvención #PodcastEnEspañol #MúsicaDesdeCasa #MamáArtista

programme.title: 🎙️ Antonio Amin, la voz de EA – 30 años de música, arte y aventuras | Momento de DESmadre Podcast
programme.desc:
En este episodio especial de Momento de DESmadre, tengo el honor de conversar con Antonio Amin, vocalista principal de EA, una de las bandas más queridas del pop-rock latino. Celebramos juntos los 30 años de carrera musical de EA, hablando de sus inicios, la evolución del grupo, el poder de la música y lo que significa vivir del arte con pasión.
💬 Temas que tocamos:
Cómo nació la banda EA La trayectoria artística de Antonio Amin Retos y alegrías de una carrera musical de 3 décadas La música como forma de vida y terapia del alma Historias detrás de canciones inolvidables 🎶 Si creciste escuchando a EA, si amas la música latina o si buscas inspiración creativa, este episodio es para ti.
🟣 Dale like, suscríbete y activa la campanita para no perderte más conversaciones con personas que viven con propósito… y con un toque de desmadre.

programme.title: Momento de DESmadre by Paula Zelaya: Un Espacio para Inspirarnos Juntos
programme.desc:
Creé Momento de DESmadre porque es mi forma de mostrarles a las personas que me inspiran, los que me hacen reír, y aquellos que, aunque piensan diferente a mí, me enseñan a encontrarme a mí misma. Escuchándolos, vemos la vida desde otros ojos. Este es un espacio para "desmadrarnos" y hablar sin filtros de todo aquello que nos hace crecer.
Quiero aprender de mis invitados y saber que su camino al éxito también ha tenido altos y bajos, pero no han dejado de luchar. Es un espacio para conectarnos y, por medio de risas y a veces llanto, inspirarnos.
Momento de DESmadre es un espacio con corazón para explorar y compartir nuestras experiencias de vida.

programme.sub-title: Behind The Blend - Lynn Hawkins Plasencia Cigars
programme.desc: Sean sits down with Lynn Hawkins of Placencia Cigars, one of the most respected names in the industry. Lynn pulls back the curtain on Placencia's extensive history as a leading grower and producer, sharing insights into their meticulous tobacco cultivation, the intricate art of their cigar manufacturing process, and what makes their family's legacy truly stand out in the world of premium cigars.

programme.title: Unrolled
programme.desc: In this episode of Unrolled, Sean Mobley visits Stogie Pairing Cigar Lounge in Fort Myers, Florida, where owners Joey and Jessica showcase their establishment, boasting 28 beer taps, 75 types of bottled and canned beers, and a full wine selection, emphasizing their commitment to diverse pairings for cigars.

programme.title: Behind The Blend
programme.sub-title: Behind The Blend - Rick Rodriguez West Tampa Tobacco Co
programme.desc: In this episode of "Behind the Blend," Sean Mobley interviews Rick Rodriguez, also known as "Chef Rick," from West Tampa Tobacco, who explains his nickname comes from blending tobacco like a chef uses food to create a desired flavor profile. Rick introduces new cigars like the "Circle of Life," a tribute to his mentors, and the "Double Crab," part of a Tampa-inspired trilogy, shaped like a "flying pig". He shares his personal journey into the cigar industry at age 40 and emphasizes that for him, cigars represent "connection" and a "gateway for a new friendship".

programme.title: Burn Rate
programme.sub-title: Burn Rate - Southern Draw Rose Of Sharon Dozen Roses Solomon
programme.desc: In this episode of "Burn Rate," hosts Bryan and Chris Kelly review the Southern Draw Rose of Sharon, Dozen Roses, a Casa de Montecristo exclusive in a Salomon vitola. They praise its craftsmanship, noting the oily, thin-veined Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper and consistent burn.

programme.title: Behind The Blend
programme.sub-title: Behind The Blend - Brian Motola And George Hadweh Cavalier
programme.desc: In this episode of "Behind the Blend," Sean Mobley interviews Brian and George from Cavalier Cigars, who discuss their roles within the company, with Brian as a partner in the Honduran factory (FBT) and George as the sales representative for Florida and Puerto Rico. Brian shares his recent full-time move to Honduras, highlighting the country's beauty and the factory's unique practice of hand-applying gold leaf to cigars, a process where empowered employees can reject imperfect products.

programme.title: Behind The Blend
programme.sub-title: Behind The Blend - Desiree Sylver Drunk Chicken
programme.desc: Established in 2019, Drunk Chicken Cigars (DC Cigars) are handmade in the U.S.A. to create premium flavor profiles. Every combination of tobacco leaf, including the filler, binder, and wrapper, was chosen to produce an assortment of smooth, rich, and savory cigars with a variety of customers in mind. Join Sean has he dicusses the mission of the DC Cigars family is to produce premium cigars that can be smoked anytime of the day.

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Hung Ga and Choy Li Fut
programme.desc: In Foshan, China, Kleber meets with two masters of southern Chinese martial arts. He learns from a Hung Ga master that while this kungfu style is often associated with brute force, it’s actually a combination of hard and soft techniques that can also be used in traditional Chinese massage. Next, Kleber meets a master of Choy Li Fut, a kungfu style that utilizes everyday items such as towels, fans and even abacuses, and discovers the link between martial arts and lion dance.

programme.title: Foodwise: Haikou
programme.desc: Welcome to Haikou, also known as the Coconut City! Join Tianran He in experiencing the unique culinary culture and urban character of this tropical paradise. From light and sweet coconut chicken hotpot to refreshing herbal desserts and spicy rice soup - a local favourite, every bite tells the story of the city's laid-back charm and beauty. We'll explore everything from Haikou's winding alleys and mangrove forests, to the culture of its southeast Asian diaspora, so come and discover this magical destination with us.

programme.title: Foodwise: Hainan's Four Famous Dishes
programme.desc: The stunning east coast of Hainan in southeast China, attract numerous visitors to travel. The reason that people tend to visit Hianan not only because of the beautiful beach view but also delicious local cuisine in Hainan. Hainan’s four famous dishes is Chicken, duck, goat and crab. In Wenchang, the ancestral home of many overseas Chinese, people could discover the original version of Hainan Chicken Rice and see how local chickens free range on coconut meat. In Qionghai, seat of the Boao Forum for Asia, you may dine on duck and goat, before feasting on crab in the surfer haven of Wanning.

programme.title: Miao Silverware: A Shining Epic
programme.desc: In this episode, we explore the fascinating world of the silver-working art of the Miao ethnic group. Join us, and hear the stories and see the works of four remarkable individuals. From a national-level inheritor who is preserving the traditional craft, to an artist infusing personal flair into his designs; from a female silversmith imbuing her work with feminine warmth, to a young artisan inspiring a new generation, we investigate the rich heritage, cultural significance, and evolving potential of Miao silverware.

programme.title: Harmony Keepers: Guardians of black-necked cranes
programme.desc: This documentary series pays tribute to the guardians of China’s rare wildlife and their habitats. Through the lens of ecological protection and preservation, the series features four iconic protected species in China: the Tibetan antelope, milu deer, black-necked cranes, and golden snub-nosed monkeys.

programme.title: China Bound: Harbin
programme.desc: Tianran He is in Harbin, the "Ice City", host of the 2025 Asian Winter Games. Internationally renowned for its breathtaking ice and snow sculptures, the city thrives with activity despite it -20°C winters. From savoring the famous local ice cream and hearty northeastern Chinese dishes such as stewed goose and sweet-and-sour pork, to drifting on the frozen Songhua River and carving down the slopse of Yabuli Ski Resort, discover how much fun you can have in Harbin.

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.4
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He travels to Shannan, the cradle of Tibetan culture. Nestled in the gentlest valley of the Yarlung Zangbo River, this is where the first Tibetan king rose to power, the first palace in Xizang was built, and many other “firsts” in Xizang’s history began. Tianran visits Yamdrok Lake, one of Xizang’s three sacred lakes, where a paragliding base is taking shape. He then learns the art of Tibetan opera, joins rangers on a mission to track the elusive Tibetan red deer, and ends the day with a rejuvenating soak in a village revitalized by hot spring tourism.

programme.title: Life as a Miao Embroidery Girl
programme.desc: In this episode, host Eva May travels to Maomaohe Village in Leishan County, Guizhou Province — a place renowned for its exquisite Miao embroidery. She spends a week immersing herself in the daily lives of local embroidery artisans, learning traditional Miao folk songs, and rising to the challenge of creating a piece of Miaoxiu embroidery with special cultural significance.

programme.title: Aerial China II Ep.6
programme.desc: The mountainous realm of Fujian's centers around the Wuyi range, just opposite Taiwan Province. Join us as we trace a heritage of tea production in ancient villages, marvel at waterside Danxia, and discover terraces where seas of lotuses grow...

programme.title: Harmony Keepers: Guardians of black-necked cranes
programme.desc: This documentary series pays tribute to the guardians of China’s rare wildlife and their habitats. Through the lens of ecological protection and preservation, the series features four iconic protected species in China: the Tibetan antelope, milu deer, black-necked cranes, and golden snub-nosed monkeys.

programme.title: Discovering the Ancient Grottoes of Chongqing
programme.desc: The third episode of the Chongqing Series, Humanistic Chongqing, focuses on the Dazu Stone Carvings in Chongqing. In 1999, the Dazu Stone Carvings were inscribed on the World Cultural Heritage List. As an outstanding representative of China's late grotto carving art, they integrate the essence of Confucianism, Buddhism and Taoism in their content, fully embodying the beauty of cultural integration. This episode comprehensively showcases the profound historical and cultural heritage of Dazu and its vibrant contemporary folk customs, exploring the thematic connotations, artistic characteristics and historical origins of the Dazu Stone Carvings, as well as their far-reaching influence on the local people for generations.

programme.desc: The mountainous realm of Fujian's centers around the Wuyi range, just opposite Taiwan Province. Join us as we trace a heritage of tea production in ancient villages, marvel at waterside Danxia, and discover terraces where seas of lotuses grow...

programme.title: Harmony Keepers: Guardians of black-necked cranes
programme.desc: This documentary series pays tribute to the guardians of China’s rare wildlife and their habitats. Through the lens of ecological protection and preservation, the series features four iconic protected species in China: the Tibetan antelope, milu deer, black-necked cranes, and golden snub-nosed monkeys.

programme.title: Discovering the Ancient Grottoes of Chongqing
programme.desc: The third episode of the Chongqing Series, Humanistic Chongqing, focuses on the Dazu Stone Carvings in Chongqing. In 1999, the Dazu Stone Carvings were inscribed on the World Cultural Heritage List. As an outstanding representative of China's late grotto carving art, they integrate the essence of Confucianism, Buddhism and Taoism in their content, fully embodying the beauty of cultural integration. This episode comprehensively showcases the profound historical and cultural heritage of Dazu and its vibrant contemporary folk customs, exploring the thematic connotations, artistic characteristics and historical origins of the Dazu Stone Carvings, as well as their far-reaching influence on the local people for generations.

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Hung Ga and Choy Li Fut
programme.desc: In Foshan, China, Kleber meets with two masters of southern Chinese martial arts. He learns from a Hung Ga master that while this kungfu style is often associated with brute force, it’s actually a combination of hard and soft techniques that can also be used in traditional Chinese massage. Next, Kleber meets a master of Choy Li Fut, a kungfu style that utilizes everyday items such as towels, fans and even abacuses, and discovers the link between martial arts and lion dance.

programme.title: Foodwise: Haikou
programme.desc: Welcome to Haikou, also known as the Coconut City! Join Tianran He in experiencing the unique culinary culture and urban character of this tropical paradise. From light and sweet coconut chicken hotpot to refreshing herbal desserts and spicy rice soup - a local favourite, every bite tells the story of the city's laid-back charm and beauty. We'll explore everything from Haikou's winding alleys and mangrove forests, to the culture of its southeast Asian diaspora, so come and discover this magical destination with us.

programme.title: Foodwise: Hainan's Four Famous Dishes
programme.desc: The stunning east coast of Hainan in southeast China, attract numerous visitors to travel. The reason that people tend to visit Hianan not only because of the beautiful beach view but also delicious local cuisine in Hainan. Hainan’s four famous dishes is Chicken, duck, goat and crab. In Wenchang, the ancestral home of many overseas Chinese, people could discover the original version of Hainan Chicken Rice and see how local chickens free range on coconut meat. In Qionghai, seat of the Boao Forum for Asia, you may dine on duck and goat, before feasting on crab in the surfer haven of Wanning.

programme.title: Miao Silverware: A Shining Epic
programme.desc: In this episode, we explore the fascinating world of the silver-working art of the Miao ethnic group. Join us, and hear the stories and see the works of four remarkable individuals. From a national-level inheritor who is preserving the traditional craft, to an artist infusing personal flair into his designs; from a female silversmith imbuing her work with feminine warmth, to a young artisan inspiring a new generation, we investigate the rich heritage, cultural significance, and evolving potential of Miao silverware.

programme.title: Harmony Keepers: Guardians of black-necked cranes
programme.desc: This documentary series pays tribute to the guardians of China’s rare wildlife and their habitats. Through the lens of ecological protection and preservation, the series features four iconic protected species in China: the Tibetan antelope, milu deer, black-necked cranes, and golden snub-nosed monkeys.

programme.title: China Bound: Harbin
programme.desc: Tianran He is in Harbin, the "Ice City", host of the 2025 Asian Winter Games. Internationally renowned for its breathtaking ice and snow sculptures, the city thrives with activity despite it -20°C winters. From savoring the famous local ice cream and hearty northeastern Chinese dishes such as stewed goose and sweet-and-sour pork, to drifting on the frozen Songhua River and carving down the slopse of Yabuli Ski Resort, discover how much fun you can have in Harbin.

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.4
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He travels to Shannan, the cradle of Tibetan culture. Nestled in the gentlest valley of the Yarlung Zangbo River, this is where the first Tibetan king rose to power, the first palace in Xizang was built, and many other “firsts” in Xizang’s history began. Tianran visits Yamdrok Lake, one of Xizang’s three sacred lakes, where a paragliding base is taking shape. He then learns the art of Tibetan opera, joins rangers on a mission to track the elusive Tibetan red deer, and ends the day with a rejuvenating soak in a village revitalized by hot spring tourism.

programme.title: Life as a Miao Embroidery Girl
programme.desc: In this episode, host Eva May travels to Maomaohe Village in Leishan County, Guizhou Province — a place renowned for its exquisite Miao embroidery. She spends a week immersing herself in the daily lives of local embroidery artisans, learning traditional Miao folk songs, and rising to the challenge of creating a piece of Miaoxiu embroidery with special cultural significance.

programme.title: Aerial China II Ep.6
programme.desc: The mountainous realm of Fujian's centers around the Wuyi range, just opposite Taiwan Province. Join us as we trace a heritage of tea production in ancient villages, marvel at waterside Danxia, and discover terraces where seas of lotuses grow...

programme.title: Harmony Keepers: Guardians of black-necked cranes
programme.desc: This documentary series pays tribute to the guardians of China’s rare wildlife and their habitats. Through the lens of ecological protection and preservation, the series features four iconic protected species in China: the Tibetan antelope, milu deer, black-necked cranes, and golden snub-nosed monkeys.

programme.title: Discovering the Ancient Grottoes of Chongqing

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Taiji Quan
programme.desc: Kleber travels to Chenjiagou in central China, the birthplace of Chen-style Taiji Quan. Also known as tai chi, the martial art is iconic for its slow movements and purported health benefits, but Kleber quickly discovers it’s the real deal: From being thrown around by teenagers to learning about the martial art’s Yin-Yang philosophy, Kleber experiences for himself how this kungfu style allows small to defeat big, and soft to beat strong.

programme.title: Foodwise: Xishuangbanna Ep.1
programme.desc: What's not to love about Xishuangbanna? From dazzling night markets to lush bamboo forests, 800-year old tea trees to close encounters with elephants, this tropical city in southwest China has everything, and is where the story of tea begins. Join Foodwise for all the Pu'er tea you can drink and feast on everything from banana flowers to "elephant food"!

programme.title: Foodwise: Xishuangbanna Ep.2
programme.desc: Come get soaked at the Dai people's New Year celebrations! We'll check out buzzing street markets packed with barbecued meats and spicy fruits, crash a foodie auction, and even take part in a rowdy competition, catching fish with our bare hands in the river. All this before hiking through an actual rainforest. We're going to need all the good tea and food we can get!

programme.title: Exploring Ethnic Attire: Dong Elegance
programme.desc: Dong clothing weaves together tradition, craftsmanship, and the unique identity of the Dong ethnic group. In this episode, we’ll unravel the stories behind the intricate designs, vibrant colors, and deep cultural significance of Dong attire. From ceremonial garments to everyday wear, each piece is imbued with the essence of a rich heritage.

programme.title: Harmony Keepers: Guardians of milu deer
programme.desc: This documentary series pays tribute to the guardians of China’s rare wildlife and their habitats. Through the lens of ecological protection and preservation, the series features four iconic protected species in China: the Tibetan antelope, milu deer, black-necked cranes, and golden snub-nosed monkeys.

programme.title: Sanxingdui: Rediscovering a Lost Civilisation
programme.desc: Sanxingdui Site is located at Guanghan, Sichuan Province. It is a site of an ancient city, ancient kingdom and ancient Shu culture in southwest of China, which is the largest in area, longest in time span and richest in cultural connotation. The total area covers 12 square kilometers, which was built over 3000 years ago. The cultural relics at Sanxingdui are precious cultural heritage of mankind, which contain rich historical, cultural and scientific value, and bespeak themselves as the most attractive ones amongst the multitude of the spectacular relics in China. In this episode, under the guide of the presenter, we visit the Sanxingdui Site Garden, archaeological Site and Sanxingdui Museum, show the amazing giant bronze mask, exquisite gold stuff, marvelous bronze divine tree etc., re-explore this mysterious and great civilization 3000 years ago.

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.5
programme.desc: In this final episode, Tianran journeys to Nyingchi, known as “Xizang’s Garden.” Here, he experiences the region’s semi-pastoral way of life — feeding yaks, trying his hand at archery, and seeing how tourism is transforming lives in Lulang International Tourist Town. Travelling along National Highway 318, Tianran discovers towering millennia-old cypress trees and rafts through the vast Yani National Wetland Park, before ending the day with a unique spa treatment at a traditional Tibetan hospital.

programme.title: Life as a Miao Silversmith
programme.desc: In this episode, Eva May steps into Maliao Village — a century-old silversmith village nestled in Leishan, Guizhou Province. Over the course of a week, she dives into the craft and daily lives of Miao men who carry on the silversmithing legacy. She works side by side with local silversmiths day in and day out, delving into the culture and techniques behind Miao silverware. She even joins master silversmiths for a live-stream event, before engaging in discussions with university professors about how traditional craftsmanship can fuel rural revitalization. On top of that, she witnesses the breathtaking sight of "maidens adorned in silver and flowers" at the grand Miao New Year celebrations, visits Xijiang Qianhu Miaozhai — the world’s largest Miao village — and learns to forge a small yet meaningful piece of Miao silver ornament.

programme.title: Aerial China II Ep.7
programme.desc: Jiangsu---an aquatic lowland stitched together by the Yangtze and Grand Canal. From Yellow Sea wetlands populated by red-crowned cranes to the Yangtze estuary's port history, this is a land and coast where maritime legends are made!

programme.title: Harmony Keepers: Guardians of milu deer
programme.desc: This documentary series pays tribute to the guardians of China’s rare wildlife and their habitats. programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Five Ancestors Fist
programme.desc: In Quanzhou, southeast China, Kleber seeks out masters of the Five Ancestors Fist, a combination of five local kungfu styles. He meets the abbot of a Southern Shaolin Temple, and takes part in the extraordinary training regime used by Shaolin monks to hone their bodies and minds. He experiences the intricacies of Quanzhou’s traditional puppetry, and learns how Five Ancestors Fist incorporated military tactics that allowed its practitioners to band together and fight off pirates.

programme.title: Living Arts of Huizhou
programme.desc: This is Huangshan in eastern China. In this city, you’ll encounter one of China’s most traditional building styles: Hui-style architecture. How does Hui style set this region apart? What’s life like for people living in these houses? With these questions in mind, we’re embarking on a journey to decode Hui-style architecture.

programme.title: China Bound：Xiamen
programme.desc: What's it like in one of China's happiest cities? Tianran is in sunny Xiamen on China's southeast coast, visiting the city's famous "island of music" and sampling local delicacies like shark meatballs, shacha noodles and fish in "soy sauce water". He'll discover former fishing villages turned hipster havens, drink tea with locals beneath traditional tenement buildings, and visit a student enclave brimming with creative startup energy.

programme.title: China Untapped: Changsha
programme.desc: The city of Changsha is one of central China's powerhouses. It's a leader in both the construction machinery industry and in media – Changsha was China's first UNESCO "Creative City". It's also one of China's best-known cities for its nightlife. The soul of a city is in its people, and this episode focuses on the women of Changsha who are helping to innovate, change and further develop this city they call home.

programme.title: Young drummer of Ansai
programme.desc: Soaring leaps and the energetic beats of the Ansai waist drum dance made Gao Yuchen, a nine-year-old boy, fall in love with the dance at first sight. Growing up in Ansai, Shaanxi, Gao was first drawn to the large-scale folk dance while watching a local performance. As a form of intangible cultural heritage, the Ansai waist drum dance was promoted by local authorities and was included as part of his school's PE program. Gao was able to receive waist drum dance training as an extracurricular activity at his school, and he subsequently became a rising star on campus. He says he wants to become a better dancer and hopes to perform on bigger stages.

programme.title: Foodwise: Huangshan Ep.1
programme.desc: Tianran and Hannah climb Mount.Huangshan, one of China's most famous mountains, sampling its delicate green tea and the rich flavors of Anhui cuisine, and explore the region's ancient villages and lush bamboo forests featured in the blockbuster film "Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon".

programme.title: Foodwise: Huangshan Ep.2
programme.desc: In Huangshan, Anhui Province, the hosts enjoy a cup of Queen Elizabeth II's favorite tea, as well as the oldest green tea to be exported Europe, and get hands on with quirky local delicacies ranging from "word candy" and tofu made of leaves, to the downright funky flavors of hairy tofu and stinky mandarin fish.

programme.title: All About the Yak
programme.desc: In this episode, we go to Nangqian, Yushu, Qinghai Province, to get close contact with the Yak in Tibet, which is known as the " Vehicle on the Plateau". During the bustling yak culture festival, people gather from near and far, meadows are crowded, and yak appraisal activities are also in full swing. As the journey continues, we are able to understand several aspects of the yak culture which is closely related to the life of Tibetan people.

programme.title: Seafaring Tales: Fu Ships
programme.desc: In past centuries, transporting goods along the Maritime Silk Road could be a hazardous undertaking. Ships often faced fierce storms which blew up on the high seas. To reduce the danger, China’s shipbuilders came up with a solution. They developed Fu ships, commonly known as junks, incorporating a special watertight bulkhead technology. Their revolutionary design allowed the ships to withstand the highest winds and roughest waters. The Maritime Silk Road was an ancient trading route that connected China to Southeast and South Asia, the Middle East, and Africa. As a key passageway for trade and cultural exchange, it thrived for well over a thousand years, bringing Chinese tea, silk, porcelain, spices, and other precious cargo to the rest of the planet. The legacy of the Maritime Silk Road is still evident today in many parts of the world.

programme.title: Shenzhen：Before and Beneath the Skyscrapers

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: White Crane
programme.desc: In Yongchun, China, Kleber explores the origins of White Crane kungfu and its effect on the martial arts world. He learns how its blocks and strikes were inspired by animal movements, and how acupuncture points can be used to deadly effect. After training his grip and finger strength with wooden sticks, he travels to Beijing for an introduction to Goju-ryu karate, and discovers striking similarities with White Crane.

programme.title: Fujian’s Tulou – The Mysterious Earthen Castles
programme.desc: The tulous, or earth-built dwellings, of Fujian are recognized as treasures of traditional architecture, thanks to their unique design, cultural importance, and embodiment of the concept of harmonious coexistence with nature. Tulous are mostly rectangular or circular in form, with a simple, elegant exterior and a well-furnished interior. As homes built by the Hakka people, they are imbued with diligence, wisdom, and the pursuit of excellence. Surrounded by mountains and waters, the tulous blend well with the natural environment. When building their tulous, the Hakka people pay attention to ecological balance in order to minimize their environmental footprint. A tulou is not only a safe place to live, but also the crystallization of the culture and architectural skill passed down for generations among the Hakka people.

programme.title: China Bound：Suzhou
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He visits Suzhou, a historic city in eastern China famously admired by Marco Polo. Crisscrossed by canals, Suzhou is renowned for its exquisite gardens, where ancient scholars recreated nature's beauty within their own homes. Tianran discovers a city of refined tastes, where even a bowl of breakfast noodles comes with unspoken etiquette, locals insist on only in-season produce, and foodies eagerly await the arrival of prized hairy crabs.

programme.title: China Untapped: Huzhou
programme.desc: Located in the east of China, on the south shore of Taihu Lake, Huzhou has been well-known for its richness in resources and blooming in silk trade since the ancient times. Guided by the concept of "lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets", Huzhou now is committed to developing green industries. In this episode, CGTN hosts Tianran He and Hannah Wilson travelled to Huzhou, where they tried a variety of guesthouse hotels in the Moganshan Mountains; experienced the life of digital nomads in Anji’s countryside; learned about the eco-concepts behind China's traditional architectures in Nanxun Ancient Town; and explored the development of eco-agriculture powered by high-tech along the Taihu Lake. All these phenomena demonstrate that economic development and environmental protection can achieve harmonious coexistence, and that civilization thrives if ecology is prosperous.

programme.title: Young dancer of Batang melody
programme.desc: Tibetan girl Tashi Badro from Batang, Ganzi, Sichuan has learned how to do the Xianzi dance both from her mom and a school program. Batang Xianzi is a unique folk dance of the Tibetan ethnic group with a history spanning over 1,000 years on the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau. In order to keep the Tibetan tradition alive, Badro’s school has offered the dance as a cultural activity. Badro said dancing with her classmates is the happiest moment of her day. Watch the graceful movements of Badro and her peers performing the Xianzi dance.

programme.title: Foodwise: Fuding
programme.desc: The hosts are in Fuding, Fujian Province in southeast China for the Dragon Boat Festival, where teams of rowers compete against each other in narrow dragon-shaped boats. From making and eating zongzi rice dumplings to trying local street food, the hosts take part in the festivities before exploring the world of white tea, from visiting its “mother tree” to drinking it in a zen temple, and even feasting on a white tea banquet!

programme.title: Foodwise: Wuyi Mountains
programme.desc: The hosts are in the Wuyi Mountains of Fujian Province, the birthplace of oolong tea. Here they enjoy tea ceremony on a bamboo raft, feast on everything from smoked goose to lotus seed soup, and explore an ancient town that once sold tea to Russia. They discover that here it’s all about terroir, and that nestled within the cliffs of the Wuyi Mountains is the most expensive tea in the world.

programme.title: The Yak and the Nomad
programme.desc: Qinghai’s Yushu Prefecture is one of China’s key yak-producing regions. This trip took us to Nangqian County, where we explored the yak industry that lies at the heart of Tibetan herders’ daily lives. Trekking into the far-flung pastoral corners of the plateau, we listened closely to the stories behind the hurdles and hopes of pastoral life and development.

programme.title: Awakening Lion-1
programme.desc: Xingshi, or literally “awakened lion,” is a name for the southern style of the lion dance. Historically, it evolved from a court dance in the Tang Dynasty almost 1,200 years ago. With the southward migration of the population from the central plains, lion dance culture was introduced to the south. In the Ming Dynasty around 400 years ago, xingshi appeared in Guangdong and was then widely spread throughout southern China and even overseas. Lion dance has become a very important part of Chinese culture.

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Wing Chun
programme.desc: Martial arts lover Kleber Battaglia is on a mission: To seek out China's kungfu masters, and learn their secrets. From explosive Wing Chun to fluid Taiji Quan, slippery Snake Style to elegant White Crane, he'll learn hidden moves and ancient techniques for defeating powerful opponents. But ?there’s more to kungfu than combat: From culture and philosophy, to wellness and insights from the natural world, Kleber will discover that contained within every kick, strike and throw, is the condensed wisdom of the ancient masters. This is Kungfu-wise. Kleber travels to Foshan, the birthplace of Wing Chun. A practitioner of this style, he seeks out masters of two different lineages: Ip Man and Snake Style. First he visits the Ip Man lineage, based on the legendary kungfu master whose life story spawned hundreds of martial arts movies, with Bruce Lee counting among his students. With Ip Man Wing Chun, Kleber learns how to create powerful short strikes perfectly suited to fighting in Foshan’s narrow alleys. With Snake Style, he experiences unique training methods that give its practitioners superhuman flexibility, allowing them to stick to their opponents, and even fight on boats in canals

From making and eating zongzi rice dumplings to trying local street food, the hosts take part in the festivities before exploring the world of white tea, from visiting its “mother tree” to drinking it in a zen temple, and even feasting on a white tea banquet!

programme.title: Foodwise: Wuyi Mountains
programme.desc: The hosts are in the Wuyi Mountains of Fujian Province, the birthplace of oolong tea. Here they enjoy tea ceremony on a bamboo raft, feast on everything from smoked goose to lotus seed soup, and explore an ancient town that once sold tea to Russia. They discover that here it’s all about terroir, and that nestled within the cliffs of the Wuyi Mountains is the most expensive tea in the world.

programme.title: The Yak and the Nomad
programme.desc: Qinghai’s Yushu Prefecture is one of China’s key yak-producing regions. This trip took us to Nangqian County, where we explored the yak industry that lies at the heart of Tibetan herders’ daily lives. Trekking into the far-flung pastoral corners of the plateau, we listened closely to the stories behind the hurdles and hopes of pastoral life and development.

programme.title: Awakening Lion-1
programme.desc: Xingshi, or literally “awakened lion,” is a name for the southern style of the lion dance. Historically, it evolved from a court dance in the Tang Dynasty almost 1,200 years ago. With the southward migration of the population from the central plains, lion dance culture was introduced to the south. In the Ming Dynasty around 400 years ago, xingshi appeared in Guangdong and was then widely spread throughout southern China and even overseas. Lion dance has become a very important part of Chinese culture.

programme.title: Shenzhen：When Travel meets Technology
programme.desc: In the second episode of the Shenzhen series, we adopt high-tech aerial shooting and follow the host on a city tour, letting audiences experience Shenzhen’s vigorous development, lush ecological scenery and cutting-edge technological strength.

programme.title: Young dancer of Batang melody
programme.desc: Tibetan girl Tashi Badro from Batang, Ganzi, Sichuan has learned how to do the Xianzi dance both from her mom and a school program. Batang Xianzi is a unique folk dance of the Tibetan ethnic group with a history spanning over 1,000 years on the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau. In order to keep the Tibetan tradition alive, Badro’s school has offered the dance as a cultural activity. Badro said dancing with her classmates is the happiest moment of her day. Watch the graceful movements of Badro and her peers performing the Xianzi dance.

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Wing Chun
programme.desc: Martial arts lover Kleber Battaglia is on a mission: To seek out China's kungfu masters, and learn their secrets. From explosive Wing Chun to fluid Taiji Quan, slippery Snake Style to elegant White Crane, he'll learn hidden moves and ancient techniques for defeating powerful opponents. But ?there’s more to kungfu than combat: From culture and philosophy, to wellness and insights from the natural world, Kleber will discover that contained within every kick, strike and throw, is the condensed wisdom of the ancient masters. This is Kungfu-wise. Kleber travels to Foshan, the birthplace of Wing Chun. A practitioner of this style, he seeks out masters of two different lineages: Ip Man and Snake Style. First he visits the Ip Man lineage, based on the legendary kungfu master whose life story spawned hundreds of martial arts movies, with Bruce Lee counting among his students. With Ip Man Wing Chun, Kleber learns how to create powerful short strikes perfectly suited to fighting in Foshan’s narrow alleys. With Snake Style, he experiences unique training methods that give its practitioners superhuman flexibility, allowing them to stick to their opponents, and even fight on boats in canals

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: White Crane
programme.desc: In Yongchun, China, Kleber explores the origins of White Crane kungfu and its effect on the martial arts world. He learns how its blocks and strikes were inspired by animal movements, and how acupuncture points can be used to deadly effect. After training his grip and finger strength with wooden sticks, he travels to Beijing for an introduction to Goju-ryu karate, and discovers striking similarities with White Crane.

programme.title: Fujian’s Tulou – The Mysterious Earthen Castles
programme.desc: The tulous, or earth-built dwellings, of Fujian are recognized as treasures of traditional architecture, thanks to their unique design, cultural importance, and embodiment of the concept of harmonious coexistence with nature. Tulous are mostly rectangular or circular in form, with a simple, elegant exterior and a well-furnished interior. As homes built by the Hakka people, they are imbued with diligence, wisdom, and the pursuit of excellence. Surrounded by mountains and waters, the tulous blend well with the natural environment. When building their tulous, the Hakka people pay attention to ecological balance in order to minimize their environmental footprint. A tulou is not only a safe place to live, but also the crystallization of the culture and architectural skill passed down for generations among the Hakka people.

programme.title: China Bound：Suzhou
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He visits Suzhou, a historic city in eastern China famously admired by Marco Polo. Crisscrossed by canals, Suzhou is renowned for its exquisite gardens, where ancient scholars recreated nature's beauty within their own homes. Tianran discovers a city of refined tastes, where even a bowl of breakfast noodles comes with unspoken etiquette, locals insist on only in-season produce, and foodies eagerly await the arrival of prized hairy crabs.

programme.title: China Untapped: Huzhou
programme.desc: Located in the east of China, on the south shore of Taihu Lake, Huzhou has been well-known for its richness in resources and blooming in silk trade since the ancient times. Guided by the concept of "lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets", Huzhou now is committed to developing green industries. In this episode, CGTN hosts Tianran He and Hannah Wilson travelled to Huzhou, where they tried a variety of guesthouse hotels in the Moganshan Mountains; experienced the life of digital nomads in Anji’s countryside; learned about the eco-concepts behind China's traditional architectures in Nanxun Ancient Town; and explored the development of eco-agriculture powered by high-tech along the Taihu Lake. All these phenomena demonstrate that economic development and environmental protection can achieve harmonious coexistence, and that civilization thrives if ecology is prosperous.

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-1 Baji Quan
programme.desc: In the first episode of Season 2 of Kung Fu Wise, Baji Quan, host Kleber travels to Mengcun, Cangzhou, in Hebei Province. There, he meets Wu Hao, the young head of the Wu-style Baji Quan school. Together, they journey across the North China Plain, from bustling village markets and the family training hall to the Bohai Sea coast, as Kleber experiences Baji Quan’s explosive power first-hand. Along the way, the episode unpacks the idea of “opening the gate”, the key to focused power, and the spirit of spear work. It goes beyond technique to reveal Cangzhou’s rich martial heritage, tracing how Wu-style Baji Quan has travelled from its hometown to Europe, proof that traditional kung fu can endure, evolve, and thrive today. In the end, Wu Hao answers with action: true inheritance is not only about skills, but about shaping spirit and character.

programme.title: Gulangyu Island
programme.desc: Gulangyu Island is famous for its exotic architecture. As a key trade port in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, it was a gathering point for merchants and diplomats from all over the world. This led to a variety of architectural styles being adopted on the island, including a fusion of Chinese and Western designs, as well as some typical of the Chaozhou region. These buildings, mostly over 100 years old, stand witness to China's reconnection with the outside world.

programme.title: China Bound: Chengdu
programme.desc: Tianran spends 3 days in Chengdu, the capital of Sichuan Province and UNESCO's first City of Gastronomy. He dives deep into Chengdu culture, exploring the infamous "mala" numbing and spicy flavors of Sichuanese street food and hotpot, and visiting historical attractions like Wuhou Shrine, Du Fu's Thatched Cottage, and the Jinsha Site Museum, which houses exquisite relics from a 3,000-year-old kingdom uncovered beneath the streets of Chengdu. Of course, no visit to this city is complete without seeing giant pandas and enjoying a cup of tea while getting your ears cleaned in the iconic People's Park. After all, when in Chengdu, do as the locals do.

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.1
programme.desc: Lhasa, set high on the “Roof of the World” in China’s southwest, is both the capital of Xizang Autonomous Region, and the spiritual heart of Tibetan culture. In this episode, host Tianran He ventures deep into the fabled Potala Palace, discovering ancient meditation caves, priceless relics and golden rooftops. Then, he tries his hand at Tibetan papermaking, learning how a poisonous ingredient is crucial for making paper that can survive for centuries. Finally, Tianran dons his apron and learns to make iconic Tibetan dishes, including one said to reveal your fortune!

programme.title: Face-changing wonder boy
programme.desc: Face-changing is an ancient Chinese performance art that is a component of Sichuan opera. Hu Yibo, 13, learned the act from his grandfather and other experienced masters. Dressed in brightly-colored costumes and while changing from one mask to another in just the blink of an eye, Yibo skillfully swipes open a fan to hide his "magical" movements. As a young inheritor, he undertakes daily training to perfect his skill set in the hope of becoming a master one day.

programme.title: Foodwise: Hangzhou Ep.1
programme.desc: In this episode Tianran and Hannah are in Hangzhou, a city with over 2000 years of history and capital of two ancient Chinese dynasties. From the famous West Lake to delicate Dragon Well tea, our hosts experience Hangzhou's must-do attractions, savouring the local cuisine and trying everything from winter melon shaped like pork belly, to food cooked according to Traditional Chinese Medicine principles, and even Buddhist noodles and Zen tea.

programme.title: Foodwise: Hangzhou Ep.2
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran and Hannah continue their tea-tasting journey along Hangzhou's Qiantang River, exploring the region's historical culture and culinary delights. They head to Anding Mountain, enjoying misty tea at the summit. In Longmen Ancient Town, they dive into traditional Chinese clan culture and savor “Sun Quan seitan”. In the gentrified village of Shishe, Hannah falls in love with “gray soup rice dumplings”, while at Qiandao Lake Tianran tries the best fish head and beluga caviar he’s ever had in his life. Their journey ends with a cup of Jiukeng tea and a visit to ancient tea trees.

programme.title: An Encounter with China’s Endangered Monkeys
programme.desc: In this episode, we head to Baima Snow Mountain Nature Reserve in Diqing Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Yunnan Province, to learn about and participate in the conservation work for the rare and precious national treasure: the Yunnan snub-nosed monkey. The presenter ventures into the forest, experiences the daily life of local forest rangers, and witnesses the harmonious relationship between humans and monkeys. We interview "the Monkey Father"—Long Yongcheng, chief scientist of The Nature Conservancy (TNC) and leader of China's Primate Expert Group—who shares stories about the two decades of efforts dedicated to protecting the Yunnan snub-nosed monkey. We also go to the mountains to conduct research alongside young volunteers. Through these activities, we recognize the importance of environmental education for young people in promoting natural ecological balance and harmonious development.

programme.title: A Lifelong Journey of Xuan Paper
programme.desc: The host travels to Jingxian, Anhui—known as the hometown of Xuan paper—to experience the intricate process of making this traditional paper. Along the way, they uncover the secrets behind its thousand-year legacy and witness the craftsmanship of Xuan paper inheritors at every stage. Through vivid, personal stories, the episode reveals the hidden struggles and quiet perseverance that have kept this intangible cultural heritage alive across generations.

programme.title: Exploring Beijing’s Backyard
programme.desc: In this episode, we explore the beautiful scenery of Beijing suburbs which is usually ignored by the public. Through self-driving tour, the representative tourism resources in the north of Beijing: Yanqing, Huairou and Miyun are involved, from the scenic spots, food to accommodation. The contents include "Mini Three Gorges" Longqing Valley, "Unique Water Great Wall": Huanghuacheng and "Northern Jiangnan" : Gubei Water Town.

programme.title: Face-changing wonder boy

As a young inheritor, he undertakes daily training to perfect his skill set in the hope of becoming a master one day.

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Pak Mei
programme.desc: In Foshan, China, Kleber seeks out Liu Weixin, a master of Pak Mei kungfu and on whom the hit game "Sifu" was based. He experiences for himself this style's relentless and lightning-fast strikes, but also learns from its master how to balance life and kungfu, how a master should treat his disciples, and what it means to "eat porridge at night"
